/books/flash-fiction/a-triangle.title: A Triangle

/books/flash-fiction/acorn.title: Acorn

/books/flash-fiction/barbara-detroit-196.title: Barbara, Detroit, 1966

/books/flash-fiction/certain-european-mo.author: Emma Cline

/books/flash-fiction/directors-cut.title: Director’s Cut

/books/flash-fiction/directors-cut.dek: Etgar Keret writes a flash-fiction story, “Director’s Cut,” about a movie that takes seventy-three years to watch.

/books/flash-fiction/good-boys.title: Good Boys
/books/flash-fiction/good-boys.author: Honor Levy
/books/flash-fiction/good-boys.dek: Honor Levy writes a flash-fiction story, “Good Boys,” about girls and boys hanging out on a rooftop in Paris, and the fraught gender dynamics among the characters.

/books/flash-fiction/gravity.title: Gravity
/books/flash-fiction/gravity.author: Etgar Keret
/books/flash-fiction/gravity.dek: Etgar Keret writes a flash-fiction story, “Gravity,” about a woman’s suicide and how it resonates with her neighbor’s feelings about, among other things, the neighbor’s own marriage.

/books/flash-fiction/grayness.title: Grayness, by Sheila Heti
/books/flash-fiction/grayness.author: Sheila Heti
/books/flash-fiction/grayness.dek: Sheila Heti writes a flash-fiction story, “Grayness,” about how the world got its colors, and what was lost when it did.

/books/flash-fiction/halloween.title: Halloween
/books/flash-fiction/halloween.author: Venita Blackburn

/books/flash-fiction/hes-very-well-read.title: He’s Very Well Read
/books/flash-fiction/hes-very-well-read.author: Catherine Lacey
/books/flash-fiction/hes-very-well-read.dek: Catherine Lacey writes a flash-fiction story, “He’s Very Well Read,” in which a woman complains about all the books a man she’s involved with keeps giving her.

/books/flash-fiction/hospice-honeymoon.title: Hospice/Honeymoon

/books/flash-fiction/i-dont-need-anythin.title: I Don’t Need Anything from Here

/books/flash-fiction/keys.title: Keys

/books/flash-fiction/listening-for-the-c.title: Listening for the Click

/books/flash-fiction/live-a-little.title: Live a Little

/books/flash-fiction/live-a-little.dek: Diane Williams writes a flash-fiction story, “Live a Little,” about a husband and wife whose kids appear to be playing happily, something the husband and wife are not doing.

/books/flash-fiction/replacement-grandpa.title: Flash Fiction: Replacement Grandparent
/books/flash-fiction/replacement-grandpa.author: Kate Zambreno
/books/flash-fiction/replacement-grandpa.dek: Kate Zambreno writes a flash-fiction story, “Replacement Grandparent,” about a mother who wishes her parents, one of whom is deceased, were more present, for both her and her children.

/books/flash-fiction/ruth-frank-and-dari.title: Ruth, Frank, and Dario

/books/flash-fiction/smithereens.title: Smithereens

/books/flash-fiction/the-facade-renovati.title: Flash Fiction: The Façade Renovation That’s Going Well

/books/flash-fiction/the-hostage.title: The Hostage

/books/flash-fiction/the-kingdom-that-fa.title: The Kingdom That Failed

/books/flash-fiction/the-mirror.title: The Mirror

/books/flash-fiction/the-south-asian-spe.title: The South Asian Speakers Series Presents the Archeologist and Adventurer Indiana Jones
/books/flash-fiction/the-south-asian-spe.author: Tania James

/books/flash-fiction/what-we-have-learne.title: What We Have Learned, What We Will Forget, What We Will Not Be Able to Forget

/books/flash-fiction/when-stars-collide-.title: Flash Fiction: “When Stars Collide”
